newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Bank of China expects to issue more HK banknotes.
newsitem.headline: Bank of China expects to issue more HK banknotes.

text.p: The state-owned Bank of China Group in Hong Kong and Macau (BOC) expects to issue more than 20 percent of Hong Kong's banknotes by the end of 1999, a senior official said on Friday.

"We project that in the coming three years, our issue of Hong Kong notes will increase...to more than 20 percent by end of 1999," Clarina Man, a deputy general manager with the bank's public relations division, told Reuters.
BOC is one of three note issuing banks in Hong Kong. The others are the Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corp Ltd, a unit of HSBC Holdings Plc, and Standard Chartered Ltd.
The BOC's share of the market stood at 10.9 percent at the end of 1996, Hongkong Bank's at 75.5 percent and Standard Chartered's at 13.6 percent.
BOC, which groups 13 sister banks, accounts for more than one-quarter of total banking deposits in Hong Kong, she said.
"In view of our 25 percent share of total deposits, there's still some room for us to raise our share in note issuing."
